title: Finite open exchange commutes with coefficient restriction and tower transitions
statement:
Let $(j:U\hookrightarrow X,j':U'\hookrightarrow X',g:X'\to X,g_U:U'\to U)$ be a cartesian open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square], and let $a:B\to C$ be any homomorphism of finite commutative rings. Use constant coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, the inverse images of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}_a$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and exact sheafified extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Let
$$\beta_B:g_B^*j_!^B\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^B g_{U,B}^*,\qquad \beta_C:g_C^*j_!^C\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!{}^C g_{U,C}^*$$
be the canonical complex-level exchanges of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], using finite constant-coefficient module pullback [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. The canonical scalar-restriction identifications for the inverse images and extensions identify
$$\operatorname{Res}_a(\beta_{C,F})=\beta_{B,\operatorname{Res}_aF}$$
for every complex $F$ of $C$-module sheaves on $U$. Under these identifications the units and counits defining the inverse adjoint mates also agree: $\beta_B^{-1}$ is the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ adjunct of
$$g_U^{-1}F\xrightarrow{g_U^{-1}u_F}g_U^{-1}j^{-1}j_!F\cong j'^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F,$$
where $u$ is the extension/restriction unit and the last map is the adjunction-compatible site-composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]. All these assertions are natural in chain maps and in $a$, including identities and composites. In particular, for any sequence of finite rings $B_{n+1}\to B_n$ and complexes $F_n$ with strict $B_{n+1}$-linear maps $F_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}F_n$, the maps $\beta_{B_n,F_n}$ and their inverses commute with every transition and define inverse maps of the underlying strict towers of abelian sheaf complexes. They also do so as towers over a ring sheaf acting through compatible maps to the $(B_n)$ coefficient sheaves. No quasi-compactness or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix a homomorphism of finite commutative rings $a:B\to C$ and a scheme morphism $h:T'\to T$. By [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the underlying sheaf of the constant-coefficient pullback $h_C^*$ is the colimit-and-sheafification inverse image $h^{-1}$, and direct image $h_*$ is sectionwise, $(h_*\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(u_h(V))$, with the action through $\rho^h$. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], the $C_{T'}$-action on $h_C^*F$ is transported through the canonical constant structure map $c_C$. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] leaves every underlying sheaf and map unchanged and composes the action with $a$. Since $\rho^h$ and its adjoint $c$ send a constant section $b$ to the constant section $b$, they commute with $a$ (a map out of the constant sheaf is determined on constant sections). So the identity maps give natural identifications $\operatorname{Res}_ah_C^*F=h_B^*\operatorname{Res}_aF$ and $\operatorname{Res}_ah_*G=h_*\operatorname{Res}_aG$. The unit and counit of the module adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ are the abelian $\eta_h,\varepsilon_h$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], which are linear for the transported actions. Hence, under these identities, $\operatorname{Res}_a$ carries the $C$-unit and $C$-counit to the $B$-unit and $B$-counit. The same holds for identities and for composites of site morphisms.

proof.text: For $j$ and $j'$, the existing pro-etale extension-by-zero lemma [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] says that extension is exact, is the left adjoint of inverse image, acts degreewise on complexes, and is compatible with restriction of scalars. Concretely, this compatibility is the identity on the direct-sum extension presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]: restriction of scalars changes only the action, while [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] sheafifies the same underlying abelian presheaf and extends the action uniquely. The adjunction is the canonical one of Stacks 03DI (sites-modules, lemma-extension-by-zero). The adjunct of $\alpha:F\to j^{-1}G$ is induced by $s\mapsto\alpha(s)$ on the summand presheaf, and the unit $u_F:F\to j^{-1}j_!F$ sends $s\in F(V\to U)$ to the image of $s$ in its summand. Neither formula refers to the coefficient ring. Therefore, under the identity identifications, $\operatorname{Res}_a$ carries the $C$-unit, the $C$-counit and the $C$-adjuncts for $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ and $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ to the $B$-ones. These scalar comparisons are natural in complexes and chain maps.

source.place: Returned Step 7, direct-sum extension and scalar-restriction compatibility; Stacks Tag 03DI, sites-modules.tex lemma-extension-by-zero, adjunction construction in the proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] with coefficient ring $C$ and with coefficient ring $B$. Its canonical map is the Beck-Chevalley exchange. Put $L_1=g^{-1}j_!$, $L_2=j'_!g_U^{-1}$, $R_1=j^{-1}g_*$ and $R_2=g_{U*}j'^{-1}$, with the composite adjunctions $L_i\dashv R_i$ of the adjunctions in Step 1 and [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. The cartesian datum gives isomorphisms $a_V:V\times_UU'\cong V\times_XX'$ and the sectionwise identification $t:R_1\cong R_2$, $t_{M,V}=M(a_V)$. This is the functoriality of the composite base-change functors in [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]. The canonical $\beta$ is the unique map $L_1\to L_2$ whose $L_1\dashv R_1$ adjunct is $t^{-1}_{L_2F}\circ\eta_{2,F}$, with $\eta_i$ the composite units. Now $t$ involves only sections and restriction maps, so it is unchanged by $\operatorname{Res}_a$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. By Steps 1 and 2, $\operatorname{Res}_a$ carries every unit, counit and adjunct of the $C$-adjunctions to those of the $B$-adjunctions, compatibly with the identity identifications. Hence $\operatorname{Res}_a(\beta_{C,F})$ has $B$-adjunct $t^{-1}\eta_{2,\operatorname{Res}_aF}$. By uniqueness of adjuncts, $\operatorname{Res}_a(\beta_{C,F})=\beta_{B,\operatorname{Res}_aF}$. Naturality in $F$ and in $a$, including identities and composites, follows from the naturality of these units and of the identity identifications.

source.place: Returned Step 7, finite exchange and coefficient restrictions

proof.text:
Keep the notation of Step 3. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], $\beta$ is invertible. Its inverse is the conjugate of $t$: its $L_2\dashv R_2$ adjunct is $t_{L_1F}\circ\eta_{1,F}$. Write $\eta_{1,F}=j^{-1}(\eta_{g,j_!F})\circ u_F$ and $\eta_{2,F}=g_{U*}(\eta_{j'})\circ\eta_{g_U,F}$. Passing from the composite adjunct to the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ adjunct applies the $g_U^{-1}\dashv g_{U*}$ bijection. By naturality of $\varepsilon_{g_U}$, the $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ adjunct of $\beta^{-1}_F$ is
$$g_U^{-1}F\xrightarrow{g_U^{-1}u_F}g_U^{-1}j^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\sigma_{j_!F}}j'^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F,$$
where $\sigma_G=\varepsilon_{g_U,j'^{-1}g^{-1}G}\circ g_U^{-1}(t_{g^{-1}G}\circ j^{-1}\eta_{g,G})$ is the mate of $t$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition](2)-(4), the inverse images of the composite morphisms $j\circ g_U$ and $g\circ j'$ are $g_U^{-1}j^{-1}$ and $j'^{-1}g^{-1}$. Their direct images are the composites, and these are identified by the cartesian isomorphisms $a_V$; on $U$ the identification is $t$. The comparison of inverse images compatible with the adjunctions is unique by clause (3), and it is the mate of this direct-image identification. So $\sigma$ is the site-composition comparison of the statement. This proves the displayed description of $\beta_B^{-1}$, and likewise of $\beta_C^{-1}$. By Steps 1-3, $\operatorname{Res}_a$ carries the latter to the former.

All comparisons above are natural chain maps by the naturality in complexes in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] and by the degreewise construction in [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Let $B_{n+1}\to B_n$ be a coefficient transition and let $F_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}F_n$ be a strict linear transition. Applying the naturality square for $\beta$ to this map, and then applying its inverse square, shows that the exchanges and inverse mates commute with that transition. Hence they assemble to inverse maps of the strict towers of underlying abelian sheaf complexes. Step 1 and the definition of restriction of scalars show that every square is linear for the compatible ring-sheaf actions, so the same maps are maps of towers over the coefficient sheaves. This proves the asserted tower, chain-map, identity, and composite compatibilities.

The statement is true and keeps the parent's coefficient category (constant finite commutative rings, small pro-etale sites). beta runs g^{-1}j_! -> j'_!g_U^{-1} as in the base-change node, and the stated inverse mate is the correct one. No qc or constructibility hypothesis is needed. Small cases checked: a=id, zero ring, U empty, U=X, g=id, one-level tower, Z/l^n quotient towers. Not a duplicate: the base-change node has one ring; the underived-compatibility node gives the same mate normalization but on the etale site; strict-tower-proper-open-calculus has one fixed ring B; and no clause of the parent is restated. Faults, both E5: step 3 transported beta summand by summand and invoked an unnamed uniqueness, and step 4 asserted the mate computation without doing it. The fix rewrites steps 1-4 only. Step 1 adds h_* and the units and counits of h^* -| h_*. Step 2 shows the units and adjuncts are ring-independent, citing the 03DI construction. Step 3 now uses the Beck-Chevalley characterization: beta is the unique map with adjunct t^{-1}eta_2, where t_{M,V}=M(a_V) and Res_a fixes t and the units. Step 4 computes the j'_!-adjunct of beta^{-1} as sigma o g_U^{-1}u_F, with sigma the mate of t, and identifies sigma with the composition comparison via clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition. I read the statement's 'canonical map' as the standard Beck-Chevalley exchange constructed in step 6 of the base-change node. The statement, stmt_deps and proof_deps union are unchanged, every step is under 2000 characters, and there is no cycle.
